add.issue.name: A code-diff bar on the ticket card, beside the ref

edit.description.md:
A small green/red bar next to a card's ref, showing the split between lines added and removed across every commit that names the ticket. Hidden entirely on a ticket with no commits — a grey line on most of the board would be noise.

Cost has to stay near zero: no per-ticket git. The server already reads the whole history once with `--shortstat` (`getCommitTimeline`, cached 5s), so one pass over that grouped by the subject's leading ref token answers the whole board in one message. The client asks on connect and on window focus, never per card.

Exact figures live in the bar's tooltip; the board itself stays a picture.

add.issue.comment.md:
Shape: one websocket message, `diff-stats:get`, answered from `getCommitTimeline`'s existing cached `--shortstat` read, bucketed by the ref each subject opens with (`collectRefDiffStats`, matching `getCommitsForRef`'s rule exactly so the bar and the Code tab can't disagree). No per-ticket git, no work on the state broadcast. The client asks on connect and on returning to the window, at most once per 10s.

The pill itself came out of `DiffStat`, which was drawing it inline, into a `DiffBar` both now use.

Bars are hidden while the board is scrubbed, for the reason the dwell clock is: they count commits up to now.

Solution: merged as PR #352 — `bdaa4dd3`, `7468f670`, `8573f44c` on main.

`collectRefDiffStats` (source/mcp/api/ref-diff-stats.ts) buckets the cached `--shortstat` history scan by the ref each subject opens with, using `getCommitsForRef`'s own matching rule so the bar and the commit list can never disagree. add.issue.name: The log's Linked commits are the repository's, not the board's

edit.description.md:
On the Roadmap board with the Code series set to `Linked`, the log lists commits linked to tickets on other boards. That board carries one ticket and none of the listed commits name it.

`useEventLog` narrows its events with `onThisBoard`, but hands `keptCommits` the every-board ref→id map App builds for the chart. So a commit line can be linked to a ticket the board does not carry — and a line's route is built from the board on screen, so it leads somewhere that board cannot go. That is S021YSM's finding, applied to events only.

The log narrows to the board on screen; the chart keeps the repository-wide map, which is what it plots.

add.issue.name: Should the chart's Linked series narrow to the board, as the log now does?

edit.description.md:
`89HF7NW` narrowed the log's `Linked` commits to the board on screen. The chart above it still reads the repository-wide map, so on a board carrying one ticket the green track plots commits the log below it does not list.

Two readings, and the call is yours:

- **Leave it.** The chart is the overview and plots the repository — the same reason `S021YSM` left foreign events in the picture and took them out of the log. The two disagreeing is already the rule for events.
- **Narrow it too.** `Linked` then means one thing wherever it is read. It would have to keep the repository-wide map while All-boards is on, which is the toggle's whole point — and that flag lives in `TimeScrubber`'s own storage, not in `App`, so the map would have to be chosen there or both handed down.

add.issue.name: A killed fetch leaves a remote-ref lock that wedges every later sync

edit.description.md:
`QR97TP3` clears `refs/heads/<stateBranch>.lock` from the common git directory, but not the sibling lock a killed *fetch* leaves there.

`git.fetch` (`git-commands.ts:59`) runs `+refs/heads/<b>:refs/remotes/origin/<b>` with `cwd = stateBranchRoot`, so a SIGKILL or SIGTERM during it leaves `refs/remotes/origin/<stateBranch>.lock` behind, and every later sync dies in `pullWithRebase` with `cannot lock ref 'refs/remotes/origin/epiq/state'`. That is the identical permanent wedge `QR97TP3` repaired, at a likelier kill point: the fetch is the longest git call in a sync, and the 10s cap SIGTERMs it by design.

`refs/remotes/<origin>/<branch>` is as unambiguously epiq's as the branch itself, so the same named-ref rule can clear it.

From a review of PR #388.

add.issue.name: The state branch's ref lock is deleted without anything establishing it is stale

edit.description.md:
`clearStaleGitLocks` (`git-utils.ts:726`) deletes `refs/heads/<stateBranch>.lock` on the strength of the sync lock's pid being dead. Nothing establishes the ref lock itself is stale, and the name promises a check the body does not make.

The scenario `QR97TP3`'s own harness change acknowledges — a node process SIGKILLed while its spawned `git` survives, which is why the test now kills the process group — produces a live orphaned `git commit` still holding that lock. The next epiq process finds the pid dead, claims `dead`, deletes the live lock and commits; the orphan then renames its own lock into place and the newer commit is dropped from the branch. Committed events with no ref left pointing at them.

The worktree-scoped `clearStaleGitLocks` confines this to a worktree epiq owns; this one reaches the shared ref store, where the failure is a lost update rather than a refused command. An mtime guard — skip a lock younger than a few seconds — would keep the wedge fix and close this.

`sync-recovery.test.ts:465` covers another branch's lock only; nothing covers a live holder of the state branch's.

From a review of PR #388.

add.issue.name: killed-sync no longer kills mid-sync, and its guard cannot tell

edit.description.md:
`P5VM0FE` moved the kill, but past the window rather than into it.

With `killAfterSyncStartMs: 0` (`killed-sync.test.ts:95`) the kill lands ~1–6 ms after the actor touches the marker — a 5 ms poll plus a 0 ms timer — which is inside `ensureSyncReady`, before any fetch, rebase or commit has run. The round setup at lines 70–80, six `runActor` syncs per round explicitly "work for ana's rebase to be partway through when it dies", now serves nothing, and the file's stated subject — recovery from the rebase and autostash a mid-sync death leaves — is exercised in no round, while the run still pays for 48 publishing syncs. The old timing missed by landing after the sync; this one misses by landing before it.

`diedMidSync` (`harness.ts:401`) cannot catch that: it only proves the actor got past `actor.ts:116`, which is written *before* `syncEpiqWithRemote` is called. So the guard the change advertises — "a kill that lands nowhere no longer passes quietly" — accepts a kill that landed nowhere, and rejects only one that landed after the whole run.

A ramp measured from the marker (say `round * 40` ms against the 186–451 ms sync the comment cites) would land inside for most rounds; a second marker written after the sync's first git command, or an assertion on state the sync left behind, would pin the premise.

From a review of PR #388.

add.issue.name: The killed-sync kill races the actor's own exit, and fails the run blaming the wrong thing

edit.description.md:
`harness.ts:377` kills the actor on a 5 ms poll plus a timer. If ana's sync returns quickly — refusing with "Another process is syncing", a refusal `killed-sync.test.ts:128` explicitly filters for, so one that does occur in this suite — the actor falls through to `fs.writeFileSync(job.reportPath, …)` (`actor.ts:153`) and exits before the kill fires.

`diedMidSync` is then false and line 101 fails the whole 900 s test with "ana's sync was still running when it was killed in round N", which points away from the cause. The report that would explain it is on disk and never read.

Reading the report when `diedMidSync === false` and surfacing its `problems`, then retrying the round rather than failing, would turn this into a retry instead of a red suite.

From a review of PR #388.

add.issue.comment.md:
Solution: PR #390, commit `5ea187b0`.

`App` builds two ref→id maps from one builder (`issueIdByRefFor`): the repository-wide one for the chart, and one scoped to the board on screen for the log, which `useEventLog` hands `keptCommits`. The chart is unchanged — it plots the repository, and whether it should narrow too is `7C92VCY`.

The scoping could not be by current board alone. Closing reparents a ticket to the global Closed board and `CLOSED_TICKET_WINDOW_MS` keeps a year of them in the payload, so that would have taken the commits of every ticket a board ever finished out of its own log — 13 of the 15 lines in the report are closed tickets. A closed ticket therefore counts for both the Closed board and the board it left: `closedFromBoardIdOf` reads the lane it came from out of its own log (the one a reopen restores it to, via the existing `resolveReopenParentFromLog`) and the API carries it as `closedFromBoardId`. Derived at read time — no new event, no migration.

Tests: `commit-link.test.ts` pins the rule including the closed cases; `log-board-scope.pw.ts` gains an e2e beside the `S021YSM` one, verified red without the fix. Full GUI e2e 207 passed, 2055 unit tests, tsc and eslint clean.
